key: Abstract Interpretation + Fractal Geometry + Sensitivity Analysis

concepts.name: Abstract Interpretation
concepts.short_description: Compute properties of programs without executing them; soundness vs completeness tradeoff; over/under-approximation.

concepts.name: Fractal Geometry
concepts.short_description: Self-similar structures at every scale; Hausdorff dimension, iterated function systems, power-law scaling.

concepts.name: Sensitivity Analysis
concepts.short_description: How do output variations depend on input perturbations? Robustness of causal estimates under model misspecification.

hypotheses.statement: Cost of soundness on self-similar sets: a reasoner that certifies decisions soundly with finite-resolution abstract cells pays a power-law precision cost whose exponent is fixed by the box dimension of the decision boundary, and the horizon-dependent sensitivity (Jacobian growth) of the dynamics adds an extra, separable term via the wrapping effect.

The abstract domain as an environment: when survival of a program/organism requires certification by a budgeted sound verifier, selection imprints the verifier's geometry (its axes, its relational shape) on the evolved dynamics; 'legibility' becomes a heritable trait.

The analyzer as a dynamical system: Kleene iteration with widening is a set-valued iteration like the Hutchinson operator; its output as a function of program parameters may have a fractal set of discontinuities, i.e., sound reasoners are brittle to perturbation in a scale-free way.

Sensitivity as attention for sound reasoning: output-width/input-width ratios of abstract transformers are a sensitivity signal that can direct where to refine an abstraction; on fractal boundaries the payoff of directed refinement is quantitatively predictable from the dimension, and sensitivity misleads when wrapping dominates.

Scale-invariant knowledge: self-similarity allows certificates proven at one scale to be transported to all others by the similarity maps, so memory of verified invariants can be stored as an IFS-like code whose size is logarithmic in the scale range.

Robustness certificates over model sets: a set of plausible misspecifications is an abstract element; for iterative (fixed-point) estimators the boundary between 'conclusion holds' and 'conclusion flips' may be fractal, so sound robustness certificates for causal conclusions have a dimension-governed cost.

Sound-precision power law: partition state space into eps-cells, propagate each by interval arithmetic for horizon T, call a cell decided iff its abstract image lies inside one outcome class. The undecided fraction scales as eps^alpha_s with alpha_s = n - D_B(boundary) when propagation is wrapping-free, and alpha_s falls below the concrete uncertainty exponent alpha_c by an amount that grows with lambda_max*T.

lenses.name: Galois-dimension ladder
lenses.rationale: Measure the dimension of the world as seen through a sound abstraction rather than through samples; divergence between the two is the object of interest.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: eps-grid of abstract cells with decided/undecided labels at resolutions 2^-3..2^-10
lenses.transformation: log-log regression of undecided fraction vs eps, paired with Monte-Carlo pair-disagreement fraction at the same eps
predictedSignals: alpha_s = alpha_c = n - D for wrapping-free maps
lenses.nullExpectation: alpha_s equals alpha_c within fit error at all lambda*T (abstraction adds only a constant factor)
failureModes: interval dependency problem from expression form masquerading as geometry
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: separates the geometric cost of certainty from the abstraction-induced cost, which box-counting alone cannot

lenses.name: Wrapping ledger
lenses.rationale: Attribute interval inflation per step to stretch versus rotation so selection or exponent shifts can be traced to one or the other.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: per-step Jacobians along propagated cells and the interval hull volumes
lenses.transformation: polar decomposition J = R S; log(hull volume / true image volume) split into rotation term and stretch term
predictedSignals: exponent gap tracks rotation inflation, not stretch
verifier-selected genomes show vanishing rotation inflation
lenses.nullExpectation: inflation explained by stretch alone (norms), rotation term ~0 after controlling norm
failureModes: polar decomposition ill-conditioned near singular maps
hull vs true volume estimated by sampling adds noise
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: distinguishes geometric legibility from mere magnitude penalties

lenses.name: Domain-imprint goniometer
lenses.rationale: If a verifier imprints geometry, the imprint must be visible as an angular preference relative to the domain's axes and must rotate when the domain rotates.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: eigenvectors / right singular vectors of evolved affine maps
lenses.transformation: angles phi mod 90 deg relative to domain axes; circular statistic R4 = |mean exp(4i phi)| and mean direction
predictedSignals: R4 >= 0.3 at domain axes for box verifier; peak shifted by the domain rotation
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: domain-rotation intervention makes the imprint causal rather than correlational

lenses.name: Analyzer-vs-program variance split
lenses.rationale: Ask how much variation in a sound conclusion is due to the analyzer's own settings versus the program being analysed.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: analysis output as function of program params and analyzer params (widening delay, thresholds, narrowing steps)
lenses.transformation: Sobol first-order and total indices over the joint parameter space
observables: share of output variance from analyzer params
predictedSignals: analyzer total index large and dominated by interactions near breakpoints
failureModes: discontinuous outputs make variance estimates slow to converge
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: quantifies reasoner-induced variability, which breakpoint counting alone does not

lenses.name: Staircase counter
lenses.rationale: Direct test of whether analyzer breakpoints form a scale-free set.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: analyzer output W(theta) on dyadic theta grids
lenses.transformation: count adjacent-pair jumps N(delta) for delta = 2^-6..2^-16; fit power, log and saturating models
predictedSignals: power law with beta in (0.2,0.9) over >= 4 octaves
lenses.nullExpectation: N saturates (finite staircase) or grows logarithmically
failureModes: too few octaves to discriminate models
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: converts 'brittle reasoner' into a scaling exponent

lenses.name: Refinement-budget exponent ratio
lenses.rationale: Adaptive refinement has an ideal exponent ratio 2/D over uniform; deviation of a policy from the ideal measures how good its sensitivity signal is.
lenses.transformation: undecided area vs budget exponents per policy; ratio to uniform and to oracle
failureModes: budget range too small to reach scaling regime
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: tests whether the sensitivity signal a sound reasoner has access to is a good attention signal

lenses.name: Kaplan-Yorke cross-check
lenses.rationale: Stock dynamical-systems lens to ensure the dimension and Lyapunov estimates used elsewhere are mutually consistent, not independent knobs.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: Lyapunov spectrum of the maps and measured box dimensions
lenses.transformation: compare Kaplan-Yorke dimension with box-count dimension of attractors/boundaries across the parameter sweep
predictedSignals: lambda*T and D_B not collinear across the sweep (|r| < 0.7)
lenses.nullExpectation: lambda and D collinear, making the M1 sensitivity term unidentifiable
failureModes: Lyapunov estimates noisy at short horizons
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: identifiability check for separating dimension from sensitivity

experiments.hypothesis: The sound undecided-fraction exponent alpha_s equals n - D_B for wrapping-free maps and falls below the concrete exponent alpha_c by an amount increasing with lambda_max*T.
experiments.mechanism: Interval propagation of eps-cells through a 2D piecewise-affine map with fractal basin boundary; a cell is decided iff its image box lies in one class.
experiments.intervention: Sweep horizon T in {2,5,10,20} and conjugate an axis-aligned map by rotation R_t, t in {0,10,20,30,45} deg (leaves D and the concrete exponent invariant but changes wrapping).
experiments.positive_control: Generalized Cantor-escape map on [0,1]^2 keeping k of 9 sub-squares (k in 4..8), label = parity of escape time; analytic D = log k / log 3; require |alpha_s - (2 - D)| <= 0.1 at t = 0.
experiments.observable: alpha_s and alpha_c from OLS slopes of log undecided fraction vs log eps over eps = 2^-5..2^-10; alpha_c from 1e5 random point pairs at distance eps per eps.
experiments.success_criterion: Positive control passes for >= 4 of 5 k; and alpha_c - alpha_s at T=10 increases monotonically in t with Spearman rho >= 0.8 across (t,T) cells and reaches >= 0.2 at t = 45 deg, while alpha_c varies by <= 0.05 across t.
experiments.failure_criterion: Positive control fails for >= 2 k (instrument invalid); or max over t of (alpha_c - alpha_s) < 0.1 (abstraction adds only a constant factor; mechanism reduces to the known uncertainty exponent); or rho < 0.5.
experiments.alternative_explanation: The gap is the interval dependency problem from how the map expression is written, not geometry; or rotation changes the effective grid alignment of the boundary rather than wrapping.
experiments.null_twin: Same rotated maps and same eps grid, but cells decided by an exact image oracle (true image polygon of the cell, computed from the affine pieces) instead of interval hulls: matches grid, map, D, class balance and horizon, destroys wrapping.
experiments.why_this_implementation: A piecewise-affine planar map makes both the true image and the interval hull computable exactly, so the abstraction cost can be isolated; no learning component is needed to test a measurement law.
experiments.size: grids up to 1024x1024 cells, T up to 20, 5 k values, 5 rotations x 4 horizons, 3 seeds for the Monte-Carlo pairs
stupid_explanations: grid aligned with the axis-aligned boundary makes the positive control trivially exact
fit window choice moves the slope by more than the claimed gap
the rotation changes basin geometry within the finite window so alpha_c silently changes
the dependency problem in naive interval evaluation, fixed by single-use-expression rewriting

experiments.hypothesis: Selection through a budgeted box-domain verifier imprints axis alignment on evolved affine dynamics; rotating the verifier's domain rotates the imprint.
experiments.mechanism: Programs = 2 affine maps on R^2 chosen by an input bit stream (reachable set is an IFS attractor); fitness = negative distance of orbit mean to a target plus a diameter floor of 0.5; survival gate = proof that the reachable set stays in S = [-1,1]^2.
experiments.intervention: Arm V: box verifier (10 Kleene steps, widening, 3 narrowing). Arm V_rot: same verifier in coordinates rotated by 30 deg (S also rotated). Mutation is rotation-invariant (A <- A + sigma * Q diag(g) Q^T with random orthogonal Q).
experiments.control: Arm T: gate = 64 random concrete runs of 200 steps stay in S.
experiments.positive_control: Arm P: arm T plus explicit fitness bonus 0.2*R4 alignment term; goniometer must report R4 >= 0.5.
experiments.observable: R4 and mean direction of eigenvector angles mod 90 deg of accepted genomes at final generation, pooled per seed; spectral radius; task fitness; box dimension of reachable set.
experiments.success_criterion: R4(V) - R4(N) >= 0.2 with permutation p < 0.01 over 10 seeds; V mean direction within 10 deg of 0; V_rot within 10 deg of 30 deg; median task fitness of V within 10% of T; effect persists within spectral-radius bins.
experiments.failure_criterion: R4(V) - R4(N) < 0.1, or V_rot direction not shifted (|dir - 30| > 15 deg), or effect vanishes within spectral-radius bins (it was a norm penalty).
experiments.alternative_explanation: The verifier penalises operator norm and alignment is a correlated side effect; or widening thresholds are axis-aligned constants.
experiments.null_twin: Arm N: arm T gate plus genome-independent random rejection tuned per generation to match arm V acceptance rate: matched selection intensity, matched concrete safety, no geometric selectivity.
experiments.why_this_implementation: A small evolving population of explicit affine programs keeps the verifier exact and inspectable; a neural policy was displaced because its geometry would not be readable against the domain axes.
experiments.size: population 100, 150 generations, 10 seeds, 5 arms (V, V_rot, T, N, P)
stupid_explanations: mutation operator anisotropy favouring diagonal matrices (mitigated by rotation-invariant mutation, checked by arm N)
verifier equals a norm penalty; alignment appears through diagonal dominance
small-population drift clusters angles in every arm
near-scalar matrices have ill-defined eigenvectors and inflate R4

experiments.hypothesis: The output of a widening-based interval analyzer, as a function of a continuous loop parameter, has breakpoints whose count scales as a power of resolution over >= 4 octaves.
experiments.mechanism: Loop x <- r R_theta x + b (r=0.9) with interval analysis: widening after 3 iterations with thresholds {+-2^k, k=-4..8}, then 2 narrowing steps; output W(theta) = width of the final box.
experiments.intervention: Vary widening delay d in {1,3,6} and threshold set density (13 vs 50 thresholds).
experiments.control: Concrete invariant width W*(theta) from a 5000-point orbit hull (expected continuous).
experiments.positive_control: Synthetic Cantor staircase function sampled on the same grids; counter must recover beta = log2/log3 = 0.63 within +-0.05.
experiments.observable: N(delta) = number of dyadic neighbours with |dW| > 1e-9 * median W, delta = 2^-6..2^-16; beta from OLS on the last 6 octaves; AIC of power vs log vs saturating fits.
experiments.success_criterion: beta >= 0.2 with R^2 >= 0.95 and power-law AIC better than log and saturating fits by >= 10 for the default analyzer, and the null twin has beta < 0.1.
experiments.failure_criterion: The last 3 octaves add < 5% new breakpoints (finite staircase), or log model wins by AIC >= 10, or null twin shows the same beta within 0.1.
experiments.alternative_explanation: Breakpoints come from the integer number of iterations to convergence changing with theta, which yields many but not self-similar breakpoints.
experiments.null_twin: Same loop and same threshold set used only as a final rounding step (Kleene iteration to 1e-12 convergence, then outward rounding to thresholds): matches output quantisation, removes widening extrapolation dynamics.

experiments.hypothesis: Width-guided (sensitivity) refinement approaches the oracle adaptive exponent ratio 2/D on wrapping-free maps but falls short as lambda*T grows.
experiments.mechanism: Quadtree of abstract cells over [0,1]^2; each step split the leaf maximising interval-image width times area among undecided leaves; decided test as in W1.
experiments.intervention: Vary horizon T in {2,5,10,20} and rotation t in {0,30} deg on the Cantor-escape family k in {4,6,8}.
experiments.positive_control: Oracle policy splitting only leaves that truly intersect the boundary (ground truth at 2^-12): gamma_oracle/gamma_uniform must be within 10% of 2/D.
experiments.observable: gamma_policy = -slope of log undecided area vs log budget B, B = 64..16384.
experiments.success_criterion: Positive control within 10%; gamma_sens/gamma_oracle >= 0.8 at (t=0,T=2) and <= 0.6 at (t=30,T=20), with a monotone decline (Spearman rho <= -0.7 against lambda*T over the grid).
experiments.failure_criterion: gamma_sens/gamma_oracle >= 0.8 at all lambda*T (then it is just adaptive mesh refinement and sensitivity adds nothing), or the positive control misses 2/D by > 20%.
experiments.alternative_explanation: Decline comes from the oracle getting relatively better at long T rather than the width signal getting worse.
experiments.null_twin: Random-leaf refinement matched to the width-guided policy's leaf-depth histogram at each budget: same cell-size distribution, no sensitivity signal.
experiments.why_this_implementation: A budgeted greedy refinement loop is the minimal agent that allocates precision; no learned policy is needed to test whether the signal is informative.
experiments.size: budgets 64..16384 leaves, 3 k values, 4 horizons, 2 rotations, 3 seeds for tie-breaking

experiments.hypothesis: When survival requires a proof by a budgeted box-domain (interval) verifier, evolved linear dynamics align their principal directions with the verifier's domain axes (4-fold, mod 90 deg), and rotating the verifier's domain rotates the alignment with it; a structure-blind gate of matched selection intensity produces no alignment.
experiments.mechanism: World: genome = two linear maps A_1, A_2 in R^{2x2} (a switched linear system; which map acts is set by an input bit each step). Per seed: R=16 runs, x_0 on the circle of radius 0.5 at angles off + 2*pi*r/16 (off uniform in [0, 2*pi/16)), S=60 steps, map index from a fixed random bit per run and step. Task fitness = lam_hat - pen, lam_hat = mean over runs of max(-5, (ln|x_S| - ln 0.5)/S), pen = 2 * sum_j max(0, s2_j/s1_j - 0.5) with s1>=s2 the singular values of A_j. Both terms are exactly rotation invariant. GA per seed: P=60 parents; each generation every parent makes one offspring by adding N(0, 0.03^2) to each of the 8 entries (conjugation-invariant, i.e. isotropic); offspring pass the arm's gate or are discarded; the P fittest of parents + accepted offspring survive (stable sort, ties keep order: parents first). G=120 generations. Initial population: entries N(0, 0.3^2), failing genomes resampled (up to 200 rounds, then any still failing scaled by 0.3) until every genome passes the CONCRETE gate (unit-disc safety on the seed's runs); exactly as world() in controls.py; this initial population is shared by all arms of a seed. Random streams: world (runs, bits, init) np.random.default_rng([seed,7]); mutation default_rng([seed,11]); null-twin coins default_rng([seed,13]).
experiments.intervention: Treatment gate = budgeted box verifier with domain angle dom. Arm V: dom = 0. Arm V_rot: dom = 22.5 deg. Verifier(dom): Q = rotation by dom; B_j = Q^T A_j Q; h_0 = (0.5, 0.5) (half-widths of the box hull of the start circle, valid in any rotated frame); h_{n+1} = max(h_0, |B_1| h_n, |B_2| h_n) componentwise, |B| = entrywise absolute value, for n = 0..29 (30 Kleene steps; boxes stay centred at 0 because the maps are linear); widening h* = 1.05 * h_30; PROVEN iff |B_j| h* <= h* componentwise for j = 1, 2 (h* is inductive, hence contains every reachable state from the start box) AND h*_1^2 + h*_2^2 <= 1 (box inside the unit disc). Offspring are accepted iff PROVEN. The treatment arms use no concrete gate and no alignment bonus.
experiments.control: POSITIVE_CONTROL and NULL_TWIN below; no separate concrete-gate arm is scored.
experiments.positive_control: Concrete gate (every state of every run within the closed unit disc; NaN/inf = unsafe) plus fitness bonus 0.1 * mean_j w_j cos(4(phi_j - dom)), dom = 0 (POSITIVE_CONTROL) or 22.5 deg (POSITIVE_CONTROL_ROT). Imprint present by construction. Implemented in controls.py.
experiments.observable: Per seed and arm, on the final population (2P maps): phi = angle of the top right-singular vector of A_j, w = (s1 - s2)/(s1 + s2); A4(dom) = sum w cos(4(phi - dom)) / sum w. Clause statistics are means over the 20 seeds. Preregistered diagnostics (not clauses): A8(dom) (same with 8 in place of 4), median rho(|A|)/rho(A), median lam_hat, mean accepted fraction.

experiments.failure_criterion: [{"id": "F1", "text": "No 4-fold axis imprint under the box verifier (M2's stated observable is falsified in this world).", "statistic": "mean over seeds 0..19 of A4(dom=0) in arm V", "comparison": "<", "threshold": 0.15}, {"id": "F2", "text": "Alignment is anchored to the world, not to the verifier's domain (the rotated verifier still aligns to world axes).", "statistic": "mean over seeds 0..19 of A4(dom=0) in arm V_rot", "comparison": ">=", "threshold": 0.4}, {"id": "F3", "text": "Reading invalid (INCONCLUSIVE, not a falsification): the verifier froze evolution.", "statistic": "mean over seeds and generations of the fraction of offspring accepted in arm V", "comparison": "<", "threshold": 0.02}]
experiments.alternative_explanation: The box verifier is effectively an entrywise (infinity-norm-like) penalty whose invariance group is the signed permutations, which contain 45-deg reflections; it may imprint an 8-fold (axes AND diagonals) or sign-pattern structure, or none on singular directions at all, rather than M2's 4-fold axis alignment. A mean A4 between 0.15 and 0.40 is INCONCLUSIVE.
experiments.null_twin: NULL_TWIN: concrete gate plus genome-independent random rejection: in generation g offspring are accepted iff concrete-safe AND u < min(1, a_ref[g] / c_g), u ~ U(0,1) from the null coin stream, c_g = fraction of this generation's offspring that are concrete-safe, a_ref[g] = accepted fraction of the compared arm in generation g of the same seed (V for S1, V_rot for S2; in controls.py: POSITIVE_CONTROL). Matches task, mutation, safety and selection intensity; has no geometric selectivity. Scored with A4(0) for S1 and A4(22.5 deg) for S2.

experiments.hypothesis: For an iteratively computed estimator (undamped Newton on a multi-root score), the set of misspecification parameters on which the estimated effect keeps its sign has a fractal boundary (uncertainty exponent alpha = 2 - D well below 1), while the same estimand computed without iteration (global maximiser) has a smooth boundary (alpha ~ 1). Because a sound certifier must leave undecided every cell that contains both signs, alpha < 1 means sound robustness certification of the sign costs a power law in grid resolution steeper than for a smooth boundary.
experiments.mechanism: Data: six unit-level treated-minus-control differences d0 = (-1.9, -1.4, -1.0, 0.8, 1.2, 1.9). Misspecification (unmeasured bias in two subgroups): g = (g1, g2) in [-1, 1]^2; group labels grp = (0, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1); d_i(g) = d0_i + g1 if grp_i = 0 else d0_i + g2. Estimand: location tau of a Cauchy model with scale s = 0.5, log-likelihood l(tau) = -sum_i ln(s^2 + (d_i - tau)^2), which has up to several local maxima because the differences form two clusters.
experiments.intervention: TREATMENT label(g): undamped Newton on the score psi(tau) = sum_i r_i / (s^2 + r_i^2), r_i = d_i(g) - tau, psi'(tau) = sum_i (r_i^2 - s^2)/(s^2 + r_i^2)^2; tau_0 = sample median of d(g) (mean of the 3rd and 4th order statistics); tau <- tau - psi(tau)/psi'(tau) for exactly 100 iterations in float64. Label = +1 if converged and tau_100 > 0, -1 if converged and tau_100 < 0, 0 otherwise; converged iff tau_100 finite, |tau_100| <= 1000 and |psi(tau_100)| <= 1e-9 (psi' = 0 or any non-finite value at any step -> label 0). Newton may converge to any stationary point (including a likelihood minimum); that is the estimator as specified.
experiments.positive_control: POSITIVE_CONTROL label(g) = index of the cube root of unity reached by 60 undamped Newton steps for z^3 - 1 from z_0 = g1 + i g2 (label 3 if not within 1e-6 of a root): a fractal (Julia-set) basin boundary by construction, measured by exactly the same pair pipeline. Implemented in controls.py.
experiments.observable: Per arm and seed: 30000 base points x uniform in [-0.75, 0.75]^2 drawn from np.random.default_rng([seed, 101]) (then from the same generator: angles a of shape (8, 30000) uniform in [0, 2*pi)); for eps_k = 2^-k, k = 2..9, partner x + eps_k (cos a_k, sin a_k); f(eps) = fraction of the 30000 pairs whose labels differ (all label values are classes, including 0 / non-converged); alpha = OLS slope of ln f on ln eps over the 8 eps; also R^2 and the slopes of the coarse (k=2..5) and fine (k=6..9) halves. Clause statistics use the median over seeds 0-4. Identical code path for every arm (controls.py measure()/fit()).
experiments.success_criterion: [{"id": "S1", "text": "The sign-flip boundary of the Newton estimator is fractal in the window: median alpha <= 0.80 (D >= 1.20).", "statistic": "median over seeds 0-4 of alpha, TREATMENT", "comparison": "<=", "threshold": 0.8}, {"id": "S2", "text": "The iteration, not the estimand, makes it fractal: the global-maximiser twin's median alpha exceeds the treatment's by >= 0.15.", "statistic": "median alpha NULL_TWIN (seeds 0-4) minus median alpha TREATMENT (seeds 0-4)", "comparison": ">=", "threshold": 0.15}]
experiments.failure_criterion: [{"id": "F1", "text": "Smooth boundary: the Newton estimator's flip boundary is not fractal in the window (M8 reads NULL here: its 'likely common case' knockout holds).", "statistic": "median over seeds 0-4 of alpha, TREATMENT", "comparison": ">=", "threshold": 0.9}, {"id": "F2", "text": "Not scale-free in the window (no single exponent; reading INCONCLUSIVE, not a pass).", "statistic": "median over seeds 0-4 of R^2 of the ln f vs ln eps fit, TREATMENT", "comparison": "<", "threshold": 0.95}, {"id": "F3", "text": "Reading invalid (INCONCLUSIVE): a boundary is nearly absent or unmeasurable.", "statistic": "min over seeds 0-4 of the smallest disagreement count over the 8 eps (TREATMENT)", "comparison": "<", "threshold": 5}]
experiments.alternative_explanation: Non-convergence (label 0) forms thin smooth bands near psi' = 0 that inflate f at small eps without being fractal; or Newton's jump from the median start is piecewise-smooth in g with many (finitely many) branches, which a finite window can mistake for a power law. The coarse/fine slope split and F2 test the second; the label-0 fraction is a preregistered diagnostic for the first.
experiments.null_twin: NULL_TWIN label(g) = sign of the global maximiser of l(tau) for the same d(g): 200-point grid on [min d - 0.5, max d + 0.5], candidates = the best grid point within 0.6 of each datum and the overall best, each polished by 30 Newton steps on l clipped to +-0.05 (only where -l'' > 0), label = sign of the candidate with the largest l. Same data, same misspecification, same estimand, same pairs; the iteration's path-dependence is removed. Verified against a 200001-point brute-force argmax (3000/3000 agree). Seeds 5-9 are a replicate used only for the twin's value on S2.
experiments.cost_estimate: controls.py 110 CPU core-s (twin dominates); treatment about 10 CPU core-s

non-converged points (label 0) form a band whose width shrinks slower than eps, faking alpha < 1 (check: the preregistered label-0 fraction and alpha recomputed with label 0 merged into its nearest-sign neighbour)
the fit window sits in a pre-asymptotic crossover (check: coarse vs fine half slopes and F2)
the boundary is smooth but long and wiggly (many branches), which raises f but not the slope; only the slope is scored, so this cannot pass S1 by itself
